summary:
**ExoSpace: Astronaut Trainer** is an interactive 2D space exploration and survival game that simulates the challenges of establishing and maintaining a human presence on Mars. Players take the role of an astronaut exploring the Martian surface, driving a rover, discovering and mining valuable resources, crafting equipment, and upgrading their research base.

The game combines side-scrolling adventure gameplay with realistic space-survival decisions. Players must manage oxygen, food, water, energy and radiation protection while responding to environmental hazards such as dust storms, extreme temperatures and radiation exposure. Mined resources can be used to craft survival equipment and improve the base's life-support systems.

ExoSpace addresses the challenge of understanding the difficulties of human exploration beyond Earth by turning complex concepts into an engaging, interactive learning experience. It encourages players to think about resource management, scientific exploration, environmental risks and sustainable living on another planet.

Developed using HTML5, CSS and JavaScript, the game features interactive 2D graphics, rover exploration, mining, crafting, missions and persistent save functionality. Its creative approach combines adventure gaming with space science education, making the challenges of future Mars missions more accessible and enjoyable.
details:
Project Details – ExoSpace: Astronaut Trainer

ExoSpace: Astronaut Trainer is an interactive 2D Mars exploration, resource-management and survival simulation developed to demonstrate the challenges of establishing a sustainable human settlement on Mars. Players take the role of a Mars mission commander responsible for managing an outpost, protecting its crew and exploring the surrounding Martian environment.

The game works through a day-and-night (Sol) survival cycle. During each Sol, players receive a limited amount of solar power and must strategically distribute it among essential systems, including the oxygen generator, greenhouse, radiation shield, research laboratory and night heater. Their decisions directly affect oxygen availability, food production, crew safety and scientific progress. At the end of each Sol, players receive a report showing the consequences of their decisions.

Beyond base management, players can explore Mars through an interactive 2D side-scrolling environment and a surface exploration map. They can operate a rover, scan and mine mineral deposits, discover underground caves, collect resources, open supply caches and craft useful equipment. Different regions introduce environmental challenges such as extreme cold, high temperatures, radiation exposure, dust storms and thin atmospheric conditions. The astronaut's suit responds to these conditions, making equipment upgrades and resource planning important for survival.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project transforms complex space exploration concepts into an accessible and engaging learning experience. It encourages players to understand the interdependence of life-support systems, renewable energy, resource utilisation, environmental protection and scientific research. It also develops problem-solving, critical thinking and strategic decision-making skills. Our intended impact is to increase awareness of the scientific, technological and sustainability challenges of future human missions to Mars.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using:

  • HTML5 for the game structure and interface.
  • CSS3 for visual design, animations and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript for gameplay mechanics, resource calculations, interactions and game logic.
  • HTML5 Canvas for rendering the 2D exploration environment.
  • Browser Local Storage for saving gameplay progress.
  • NASA's DONKI API for accessing solar flare information, with archived data available as a fallback.
  • NASA scientific resources for educational information about MOXIE, space-based plant growth, radiation measurements and Martian environmental conditions.

The game is designed to run in a modern web browser on computers and touchscreen devices without requiring specialised hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Our project combines a strategy-based Mars settlement simulator with adventure-style exploration, rover operations, mining, crafting and environmental survival. Rather than simply presenting scientific information, it allows players to experience simplified versions of the decisions that a future Mars mission might face. The combination of NASA-related scientific information, interactive gameplay, changing environmental conditions and resource-based progression makes the project both educational and entertaining.

Factors Considered During Development

We considered scientific relevance, limited energy availability, life-support requirements, radiation protection, environmental hazards, resource scarcity, crew safety, accessibility and gameplay balance. We also designed the experience to be understandable for players without advanced scientific knowledge while maintaining meaningful decisions and challenges.

ExoSpace aims to make the possibilities and challenges of human exploration beyond Earth easier to understand through interactive learning and creative gameplay.
